\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು} (tolagisu)}{ತೊಲಗಿಸು (tolagisu)}]{\kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು} (tolagisu) — to get rid of}

\label{lesson:KA-C426-tolagisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for valid, then the Kannada for recognition.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು}} — \emph{tolagisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to get rid of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಊರಿನವರು} \kn{ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ} \kn{ಕೆರೆಯ} \kn{ಕಸವನ್ನು} \kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ūrinavaru oṭṭāgi kereya kasavannu tolagisidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Together the townspeople got rid of the rubbish in the lake.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸಿದೆ}, \emph{tolagiside}.

\kn{ತೊಲಗು}, to go away, to get lost.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು}} (\emph{tolagisu}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3519 lists Kannada \emph{tolagu}, \textquotedblleft{}to go away, to depart\textquotedblright{}, and its causative \emph{tolagisu}, beside Tamil \emph{tolai}, \textquotedblleft{}to perish, to be removed\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolagisu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolagisu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūrinavaru oṭṭāgi kereya kasavannu tolagisidaru.} — Together the townspeople got rid of the rubbish in the lake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for valid, then the Kannada for recognition, then say \emph{tolagisu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತೊಲಗಿಸು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get rid of\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು} (kaḍegaṇisu)}{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು (kaḍegaṇisu)}]{\kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು} (kaḍegaṇisu) — to disregard; to overlook}

\label{lesson:KA-C426-kadeganisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for recognition, then the Kannada for to get rid of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು}} — \emph{kaḍegaṇisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to disregard; to overlook\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳು} \kn{ಹಳ್ಳಿಯ} \kn{ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳನ್ನು} \kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{adhikārigaḷu haḷḷiya samasyegaḷannu kaḍegaṇisidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The officials disregarded the village's problems.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸಿದೆ}, \emph{kaḍegaṇiside}.

What is disregarded takes -\kn{ಅನ್ನು}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು}} (\emph{kaḍegaṇisu}) is built as a compound whose first part is native \emph{kaḍe}, \textquotedblleft{}end, a low or inferior place\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1109), as in \kn{ಕಡಿಮೆ}; the second part looks like \kn{ಗಣಿಸು}, \textquotedblleft{}to count\textquotedblright{}, but how the word was formed is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḍegaṇisu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḍegaṇisu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adhikārigaḷu haḷḷiya samasyegaḷannu kaḍegaṇisidaru.} — The officials disregarded the village's problems.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for recognition, then the Kannada for to get rid of, then say \emph{kaḍegaṇisu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕಡೆಗಣಿಸು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To disregard; to overlook\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ} (jāgarūka)}{ಜಾಗರೂಕ (jāgarūka)}]{\kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ} (jāgarūka) — careful; watchful}

\label{lesson:KA-C426-jagaruka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to get rid of, then the Kannada for to disregard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ}} — \emph{jāgarūka} — \textquotedblleft{}careful; watchful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ರಾತ್ರಿ} \kn{ವಾಹನ} \kn{ಓಡಿಸುವಾಗ} \kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕರಾಗಿ} \kn{ಇರಬೇಕು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rātri vāhana ōḍisuvāga jāgarūkarāgi irabēku.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
One must be careful when driving at night.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕತೆ}, caution.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ}} (\emph{jāgarūka}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{jāgarūka}, \textquotedblleft{}wakeful, watchful\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāgarūka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāgarūka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rātri vāhana ōḍisuvāga jāgarūkarāgi irabēku.} — One must be careful when driving at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to get rid of, then the Kannada for to disregard, then say \emph{jāgarūka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಜಾಗರೂಕ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Careful; watchful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತೊಡಕು} (toḍaku)}{ತೊಡಕು (toḍaku)}]{\kn{ತೊಡಕು} (toḍaku) — a snag; a complication}

\label{lesson:KA-C426-todaku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to disregard, then the Kannada for careful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತೊಡಕು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತೊಡಕು}} — \emph{toḍaku} — \textquotedblleft{}a snag; a complication\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಮನೆ} \kn{ಕಟ್ಟುವಾಗ} \kn{ಹಲವು} \kn{ತೊಡಕುಗಳು} \kn{ಬಂದವು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mane kaṭṭuvāga halavu toḍakugaḷu bandavu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many snags came up while building the house.
\end{quote}

Plural: \kn{ತೊಡಕುಗಳು}, \emph{toḍakugaḷu}.

\kn{ತೊಡಕಾಗು}, to become a hitch.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತೊಡಕು}} (\emph{toḍaku}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3480 lists Kannada \emph{toḍaku}, \emph{toḍaṅku}, \textquotedblleft{}to get entangled, to be caught\textquotedblright{}; a snag is what one gets caught on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{toḍaku}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{toḍaku}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mane kaṭṭuvāga halavu toḍakugaḷu bandavu.} — Many snags came up while building the house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to disregard, then the Kannada for careful, then say \emph{toḍaku} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತೊಡಕು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A snag; a complication\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ} (pratikūla)}{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ (pratikūla)}]{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ} (pratikūla) — adverse; unfavourable}

\label{lesson:KA-C426-pratikula}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for careful, then the Kannada for a snag.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ}} — \emph{pratikūla} — \textquotedblleft{}adverse; unfavourable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ} \kn{ಹವಾಮಾನದಿಂದ} \kn{ವಿಮಾನ} \kn{ತಡವಾಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pratikūla havāmānadinda vimāna taḍavāyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight was delayed by bad weather.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಅನುಕೂಲ} is its opposite.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ}} (\emph{pratikūla}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{pratikūla}, \textquotedblleft{}against the bank\textquotedblright{}, so \textquotedblleft{}contrary, adverse\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8545).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratikūla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratikūla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratikūla havāmānadinda vimāna taḍavāyitu.} — The flight was delayed by bad weather.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for careful, then the Kannada for a snag, then say \emph{pratikūla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
